review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] attributes and no simp calls. It defines envelope functions as plain defs. It proves monotonicity through hand-composed `0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ a'` bounds (`bound_add`, `bound_mul`, `bound_pow`, `bound_refl`) and `unfold`. I checked downstream uses of these defs. `TransverseHistoryParentCost.lean` and `ParentHistoryCostPolynomial.lean` use `unfold` and `simp only [..., parentDifferenceEnvelope, differenceEnvelope, ...]`. That is explicit, terminating unfolding. I found no concrete expression whose normal form is wrongly handled. I found no competing rules and no credible rewrite cycle. Adding simp lemmas for these defs would be speculative. Recommending simp annotations on these definitions or bound lemmas would only be justified by how an identity looks, which the rubric rules out. I did not review the proof-automation style of the `bound_*` combinators, because that falls under other rubrics. I could not run Lean, so I did not test simp behaviour.
